    Docs / UpgradingSource: docs/UPGRADING.md

    Upgrading wayu

    User-visible behavior changes per release. A release names the "Unreleased" section after its version and publishes it as the GitHub release's "⚠ Upgrade notes"; CHANGELOG.md also lists the breaking commits' BREAKING CHANGE: footers. 4.4.3 and 4.4.4 shipped behavior changes as patch releases, so they are listed here too.

    Unreleased#

    Prebuilt binaries for Intel Macs and Linux on arm64#

    • Releases now ship wayu-macos-amd64 (macOS 15 or later on Intel) and wayu-linux-arm64 next to wayu-macos-arm64 and wayu-linux-amd64, each with a .sha256 and a build provenance attestation. brew install wayu picks the right one; it no longer refuses those two platforms.

    Multi-machine secrets (experimental, opt-in)#

    • New: wayu secrets identity, wayu secrets recipient list|add|rm|rename, wayu secrets adopt --yes, wayu secrets recovery add|rm|unlock. They let several machines read the same synced secrets.json without copying a key: each machine has its own age identity and the data key is wrapped to each. Marked experimental (see docs/STABILITY.md): they print a one-time notice the first time.
    • Nothing changes until you opt in. The first recipient add (or recovery add) rewrites secrets.json to version 2 (backup first, verified, one-time notice). wayu 7.0 cannot read version 2 (it exits 78 and, from this release on, names the upgrade): upgrade wayu on every machine that syncs the file before you run it.
    • wayu doctor warns when secret.key / identity.key sits in a git work tree without being ignored, and about sync-conflict copies of secrets.json (secrets.sync-conflict-*.json, secrets 2.json).
    • A new machine never trusts a data key by itself: after recipient add (which prints the key's fingerprint) and a sync, run wayu secrets adopt --yes there and compare the fingerprint it prints. Until then it exits 78 naming that command (at shell start: one secrets not loaded line).
    • A machine that has read version 2 keeps what it verified with its cached key (in the same keychain item or secret.key; wayu 7.0 cannot read that item). From then on a version 1 secrets.json (downgrade) or one under a key it replaced (rollback) exits 78 naming the fix, and a rotation that lists a machine it saw removed is not adopted automatically.
    • recipient add / recovery add no longer name this machine after an empty or IP-address hostname: they exit 64 asking for --name.

    secrets.json from a newer wayu: "upgrade wayu", not "malformed"#

    • A secrets.json whose "version" is higher than this wayu reads (a store a newer wayu wrote, e.g. on another machine syncing the data dir) now fails with secrets.json version N was written by a newer wayu …: upgrade wayu on this machine instead of a generic "unsupported version" or "unknown field" error. The exit code is unchanged (78) and the file is never touched.

    7.0.0#

    Leftover [paths] / [aliases] / [env] in wayu.toml are reported by build#

    • wayu build warns (stderr) for each of these tables still in wayu.toml: wayu does not read them (wayu path|alias|const add manage those entries). Before, only toml validate and doctor said so, and a hand edit there was silently ignored.
    • The prompt hook's rebuild (after a hand edit of wayu.toml / entries.json) no longer discards its stderr: its warnings and errors show in the terminal once, at that prompt. A clean rebuild prints nothing.

    completions generate: no setup instructions#

    • wayu completions generate no longer prints fpath / source / symlink steps for .zshrc and friends: wayu's init already loads its completions dir in zsh, bash and fish. It prints one line (open a new shell).

    doctor: unregistered plugin folders#

    • wayu doctor warns about folders under <data>/plugins that no plugins.json entry points at: only registered plugins load, so such a checkout is silently ignored otherwise (see "Generated shell code and startup"). Register it (wayu plugin add) or delete it.

    Aliases may use command names#

    • alias add cd z, alias add cat bat and other aliases named like a command (cd, pwd, echo, test, true, false were refused) are accepted. Shell grammar words and declaration builtins (local, export, typeset, return, ...) are still refused.

    macOS 15 or later#

    • Release binaries require macOS 15 (Sequoia) or later; the Homebrew formula says so. README lists the tested platforms and shell versions.

    Generated shell code and startup#

    • core.<ext>: the Secrets section runs after the PATH apply, and its cache-miss wayu secrets cache call (like the prompt hook's wayu build) uses wayu's absolute path, also when wayu was run by bare name from PATH (was a bare wayu, not found in shells with a minimal PATH: cron, GUI apps, ssh commands). Run wayu build once to regenerate.
    • The prompt hook's wayu build (after a hand edit of wayu.toml / entries.json) no longer compiles stale scripts while the prompt waits: it starts wayu script build in the background (a Swift script froze the prompt for ~10 s).
    • wayu build regenerates plugins.<ext> from plugins.json for every set-up shell (a hand edit, e.g. disabling a plugin, had no effect until a wayu plugin command ran), and exits 78 naming the file when plugins.json is invalid (was silent, exit 0); the plugin loaders are then kept as they were. plugins.<ext> no longer has a # Last updated line.
    • core.zsh no longer sources plugins/zsh-autosuggestions / plugins/zsh-syntax-highlighting on its own when their checkouts exist: only plugins enabled in plugins.json load (wayu plugin disable had no effect on those two). A checkout not registered in plugins.json is no longer loaded: register it with wayu plugin add.
    • Plugin *.zsh sources are compiled to .zwc next to them (zsh loads the digest instead of parsing the source each start): plugin checkouts get .zwc files (untracked in their git checkouts).
    • bash: a [tools] word zsh / --zsh in args becomes bash / --bash in core.bash, as fish already did (args = "init zsh" put zoxide init zsh into core.bash; bash 3.2 failed on its output). In core.zsh, bash / --bash likewise become zsh / --zsh.
    • [tools] entries are emitted in wayu.toml file order (were sorted by name), so a tool can rely on one listed above it.
    • bash: the [tools] evalcache helper no longer aborts a shell running with set -e when a tool is missing, fails or its cache can't be written (a failing tool now returns 0), and on bash 3.2 finds tools by walking PATH in the shell instead of one $(type -P …) fork per tool.
    • core.bash: the functions/*.bash and completions/*.bash(-completion) loops glob with failglob off and globbing on (restored before the files are sourced): shopt -s failglob printed "no match" on every start and set -f skipped the files. The loop variable is _wayu_f (core.bash left a global f behind).
    • Live PATH sync: when the prompt hook's wayu build fails (a malformed hand save of wayu.toml / entries.json), open shells retry after the next save of either file instead of never again; the hook records the failure in <data>/path_sync.<ext>.regen-failed.
    • zsh: zsh -l -c … and zsh -l -i -c … (IDEs reading the login env, ssh commands) get wayu's PATH order back before the command runs; the restore after macOS path_helper only happened at the first prompt, which these never draw. core.zsh sets a self-removing TRAPDEBUG for such runs only, and not when a TRAPDEBUG is already defined.
    • [prompt] / [prompt.*] are read with the TOML parser like the rest of wayu.toml (were matched line by line): comments are ignored (a # success_symbol = … line was applied), keys count only in their own table (a success_symbol in any [prompt.*] table was used), values of the wrong type keep the default (context_aware = "false" turned it off; toggle_enabled = true # not false read as false), and dotted keys, [prompt.contexts.<name>] tables and multi-line strings work.
    • Native prompt: a % in the git branch, the local IP, a context's tool version or the shell name is shown as is (it was expanded as a prompt escape: a branch feat%n showed the user name), in the prompt and the async right prompt.
    • Native prompt (vi mode): R (replace) and r (replace one character, while it waits for the key) show vimcmd_replace_symbol in the replace color; they showed the insert / normal symbol.
    • Native prompt (async_rprompt): the background worker starts only in a git work tree or in a context with a version command (rust, nodejs, …); elsewhere the right prompt and $version are cleared without forking. The USR1 handler no longer forks (read + zf_rm instead of $(<f) + rm): a render outside a repo forks 0 times (was 2), inside a repo once (the worker). Run wayu build once to regenerate.
    • wayu export --check compares turbo.<ext> with what export --turbo would write now, instead of its mtime with wayu.toml / entries.json: it now reports stale after a change to config.<ext>, a hand edit of the turbo file or a wayu upgrade that changes the generated code, and no longer after a save of wayu.toml that changed nothing.
    • fish: [prompt] enabled = true now generates a native prompt in core.fish (fish_prompt, and fish_right_prompt with async_rprompt): it replaces a fish_prompt from ~/.config/fish/functions/ (one defined later in config.fish or a plugin still wins); vi_mode = true switches to fish_vi_key_bindings and empties fish_mode_prompt. See config-reference "Prompt in fish". A fish setup with [prompt] enabled that relied on fish ignoring it should remove the table.
    • fish: wayu export (--turbo, --eval, --check) works for fish (it exited 64): turbo.fish is core.fish followed by tools.fish / extra.fish (same as sourcing init.fish) and is kept current by every regeneration; --eval prints fish code for wayu export --eval | source.
    • wayu build profile times core and its phase breakdown in an interactive shell that reads only core (zsh: ZDOTDIR = a private temp dir; bash: --rcfile), not -c: compinit, the native prompt and the plugins are now included, so the numbers are higher (and real). The first scenario is labeled core.<ext> (interactive, no user rc).

    wayu's own completions: position-independent, value completion#

    • The zsh, bash and fish completions for wayu parse the command line: a global flag before the command (wayu --dry-run alias rm <TAB>) or between command and action no longer breaks them, command flags complete after the action too, and -- ends the flags. They complete the values of --shell, --source, --lang, --category/-c and --template, backup types and backup numbers, template apply and plugin add names, secrets run secret names and the command after --. bash: the action position offers actions only (flags on -<TAB>); fish: the script is one __wayu_complete function (was one complete line per word). Run wayu completions generate to rewrite the scripts.

    Encrypted secrets hardening#

    • secrets.json is read strictly: unknown fields, text after the object, names that are not shell variable names, non-string values and run_only names missing from values (or listed twice) are errors (exit 78 naming the file) instead of being ignored. wayu never writes such a file; only a hand edit is affected.
    • The master key in the macOS keychain / Secret Service is stored per data dir: account wayu-<id> (keychain service wayu-master-key; Secret Service service wayu), where <id> is the 16-hex id wayu doctor prints. The old shared item (account wayu / account master) is moved automatically: the first wayu command that needs the key (a new shell, const get, doctor) copies it to wayu-<id> when it decrypts this data dir's secrets.json, and prints a one-line notice once. The old item is kept (another data dir may still use it); the notice names the command that deletes it (security delete-generic-password -a wayu -s wayu-master-key / secret-tool clear service wayu account master).
    • Secrets session cache: with neither XDG_RUNTIME_DIR nor TMPDIR set it lives in <data>/run/wayu-<uid>/ (was /tmp/wayu-<uid>/). core.<ext> sources it only from a dir you own that is not a symlink (otherwise from <data>/run/wayu-<uid>/) and never through a symlinked cache file; wayu secrets cache replaces such a link instead of writing through it. Regenerate core (wayu build) to get the new loader.
    • wayu backup restore entries (and TUI undo) also restores secrets.json as it was when that backup was taken (a copy is now kept with every entries.json backup in backup/secrets/); before, only entries.json was restored and secret markers and values could drift apart. secrets rekey drops those copies.
    • wayu const get NAME exits 65 with an error when entries.json marks NAME secret but secrets.json has no value for it (printed an empty line and exited 0). wayu doctor reports that as an error (secrets pairing, exit 78) and a secrets.json value without a secret entry in entries.json as a warning.
    • TUI constants view: encrypted constants are listed as ******** (secret) / ******** (secret, run-only) (were rows with an empty value), also after v; the TUI never decrypts them. e on one shows a hint to change it with wayu const add NAME --secret instead of opening the form; d removes it like wayu const rm (the entries.json entry and the secrets.json value together). A malformed secrets.json during a TUI add/delete is shown as an error instead of ending the TUI.
    • wayu reload / wayu watch also watches secrets.json (also before the first secret creates it): a change, e.g. by a sync, drops the secrets session cache and regenerates the init files. Any watched file that appears or is removed while the watcher runs now counts as a change (was ignored).

    One status icon per line#

    • path add / path remove print ✓ Added to PATH: <dir> / ✓ Removed from PATH: <name> (no extra ✅). plugin check / plugin update put the indent before the line's icon and drop the second one ( ✓ Up to date, ℹ Update available: a → b, ⚠ Failed to check remote …). Scripts matching the old text with the emoji need updating.

    zsh startup: interactive-only parts skipped in non-interactive shells; compinit guard#

    • Non-interactive zsh (zsh -c, scripts; wayu loaded from .zshenv) no longer loads plugins (plugins.zsh, plugins/config.zsh) or sets up zsh-defer; zsh-defer is a no-op there (nothing ever drained its queue outside a prompt). Constants, secrets, PATH, functions/, [tools], tools.zsh, extra.zsh and aliases still load. zsh -c true with a typical setup: ~20 ms → ~8 ms.
    • After wayu's compinit, a later compinit call (an installer's autoload -Uz compinit && compinit in .zshrc) no longer redoes the completion setup: it only registers the completions of fpath dirs added since, ignoring its flags; the same registration runs at the first prompt. [settings] compinit_guard = false restores zsh's own compinit.
    • .zcompdump is also rebuilt when any fpath dir (or its mtime) changed, so completions installed into brew's/the system's fpath dirs show up in the next shell (were only picked up after wayu's own completions changed).
    • zsh-defer runs queued commands once the prompt is drawn and the line editor is idle (a zle -F handler), one per idle moment, with errors shown (they were run from a precmd hook, before the prompt was drawn, with stderr discarded). wayu no longer defines TRAPUSR1 for it; with the native prompt's async data, a TRAPUSR1 function defined before wayu is kept and called first.
    • Native prompt: PROMPT is $'\n''${_WAYU_PS1}', rendered in the shell (precmd, and before the vi-mode / toggle / async zle reset-prompt) instead of two $(...) subshells per render. _wayu_prompt_full and _wayu_prompt_transient set REPLY instead of printing; {localip} is looked up once per prompt.
    • Re-sourcing init.zsh / init.bash in a shell skips plugins already loaded in it (plugins.<ext> guards each plugin) and doesn't add wayu's completions dir to fpath again or rerun compinit.
    • New opt-in [settings] keys (zsh): defer_plugins (load plugins after the first prompt) and lazy_compinit (compinit on the first completion).
    • New opt-in [settings] autosuggest = true (zsh): history suggestions (falling back to a PATH command name for a first word history doesn't match) built into core.zsh (one redraw hook, 13 accept widgets wrapped instead of every widget), styled by autosuggest_style (default "fg=8"), accepted with →/End/^F/^Y (autosuggestions_accept_keys). While it is on, the zsh-autosuggestions plugin is not loaded and wayu doctor warns if it is still enabled. Off by default: nothing changes unless you set it.
    • New opt-in [settings] highlight = true (zsh): syntax highlighting built into core.zsh (one redraw hook, no widget wrapped, nothing forks; zsh's own lexer; a keystroke at the end of the line re-highlights only the last words). Styles use zsh-syntax-highlighting's names and defaults, changed with highlight_styles = { command = "fg=blue", ... } (or a [settings.highlight_styles] table). While it is on, the zsh-syntax-highlighting and fast-syntax-highlighting plugins are not loaded and wayu doctor warns if one is still enabled. Off by default.
    • Built-in highlighting, checked against fast-syntax-highlighting (tests/highlight_diff): brackets are colored by depth (new styles bracket-level-1..3, bracket-error for unmatched ones, cursor-matchingbracket for the pair of the one under the cursor), history expansions (!!, !$, ...: history-expansion), in after case and always are reserved words, assignments after typeset / local / export / readonly are assign, command -v NAME highlights NAME as a command, nothing is a glob after noglob, =cmd is a command, a quoted command name is colored as the command, {fd} in {fd}>file is named-fd (default none; was redirection) and the descriptor in 2>&1 is numeric-fd (default none). Fixed: '...' followed by more text in the same word was colored to the end of the word, &! lost the rest of the line, $[...] was a glob, for x (...) / for ((...)), function name { ... }, case (pattern), name=(...) inside $(...), and a stale result after deleting part of a heredoc operator. Lines entered at a continuation prompt are now highlighted with the current line, and an edit in the middle of a long line no longer re-highlights it all (500 characters: ~4 ms → ~0.9 ms per keystroke). To keep the old look, set the new styles to "none" in [settings] highlight_styles.

    wayu optimize: installer lines in your startup files move into wayu#

    • New wayu optimize [--check] [--dry-run] [--yes] (see docs/cli.md): lines after the one that loads wayu (source <(tool completion zsh), eval "$(tool init zsh)", fpath=(dir $fpath), a second compinit, export PATH=dir:$PATH, alias, export NAME=value) are moved into wayu and removed from the file (backed up first; wayu backup restore .zshrc --yes undoes it). It needs --yes like other commands that rewrite files; without it (or with --dry-run) it shows the diff.
    • entries.json has two new optional sections, fpath (zsh completion dirs, put on fpath before compinit) and generators (cached _wayu_evalcache calls, emitted in that shell's core only, interactive shells only for zsh/bash). New wayu completions fpath [list|add|rm].
    • Generated core.<ext> has a new prompt hook, _wayu_rc_check: when a startup file is newer than <data>/rc_check.stamp it runs wayu optimize --notify once and prints wayu: ~/.zshrc changed: N lines can be optimized (wayu optimize) on stderr (once per change; the first prompt after upgrading checks once). [settings] auto_optimize = true moves the lines instead.
    • wayu doctor has a new "startup files" check (warning, with an estimated cost per shell start; generator commands are not run, they are listed as "runs a command every start"), and doctor --fix --yes runs wayu optimize.
    • wayu backup restore accepts a shell startup file (.zshrc, .bashrc, ~/.config/zsh/.zshrc, or its path).
    • wayu config scan reads the current shell's rc file ($ZDOTDIR/.zshrc when ZDOTDIR is set; .bashrc/.bash_profile for bash, config.fish for fish) instead of always ~/.zshrc, so --fix writes the blocks to the matching extra.<ext>; it detects # >>> … # <<< installer blocks (conda) as one block, and no longer takes a backup of extra.<ext> when it has nothing to add.

    Hooks: run outside the lock, with a timeout, output shown#

    • Hooks no longer run under wayu's config lock (pre-hooks before it is taken, post-hooks after it is released), so a hook may run wayu (a path add or plugin add hook calling wayu build hung forever).
    • Every hook is killed after 30 s (with its child processes; the CLI prints a warning naming it). timeout = <seconds> in hooks.conf changes it.
    • CLI hooks now share wayu's stdout and stderr (their output was discarded); stdin is /dev/null. Redirect inside the hook to keep it quiet.
    • pre/post_alias_remove and pre/post_constant_remove now get the removed alias command / constant value as {value} (was empty; still empty for an encrypted secret).
    • A hook command's quotes are removed only when one quoted string wraps the whole command: post_path_add = "/bin/echo" {path} "done" is kept as written (it lost its first and last quote, and every write exited 78).
    • wayu function add with no $EDITOR/$VISUAL and no terminal prints the new file's path and exits 0, like script new (it ran vi and exited 1).

    Entry names and values#

    • Alias names follow one rule everywhere (alias add, the TUI, templates, entries.json): printable ASCII except whitespace, quotes, shell metacharacters, glob characters, =, / and ^, not starting with -. .., g.st and 1x are now accepted; . and the words in "Aliases may use command names" above are still refused.
    • const add refuses protected names with exit 65: PATH, path, FPATH, fpath, HOME, IFS, SHELL, USER, LOGNAME, PWD, OLDPWD, ZDOTDIR, SHLVL, _ and every WAYU_* name (also with --secret). wayu doctor reports stored ones as an error (exit 78); remove them with wayu const rm NAME.
    • A value with a NUL byte or invalid UTF-8 (alias command, constant value, PATH dir) is one data error, exit 65 (was two messages and exit 74).
    • entries.json is read strictly: anything after the document, a trailing comma, a duplicate key, "version": "1", an unknown field, a missing value, a run_only without secret, an invalid alias / constant name or PATH key, or a NUL character now makes every command exit 78 naming the file (these were read silently, unknown fields dropped on the next write, a NUL written raw into core.<ext>). Fix the file by hand or wayu backup restore entries --yes.

    Directories and the lock#

    • A relative WAYU_CONFIG_DIR or WAYU_DATA_DIR makes every command exit 78 (it was used as-is, relative to each process's working directory). Use an absolute path.
    • The config lock is always <data>/.wayu.lock: the first writing command creates the data dir if it is missing (it used to lock in the config dir, or not at all, before the data dir existed, and concurrent first writes lost entries). A leftover ~/.config/wayu/.wayu.lock can be deleted.

    PATH entries must be directories#

    • wayu path add of an existing path that is not a directory (/etc/hosts) exits 65 (it was stored). A missing path still exits 66.
    • wayu template apply / init --template add only PATH dirs that exist and are directories (others are listed as kept out: "not on this machine"); they were added whether or not they existed.

    wayu watch stop / status check the watcher's lock#

    • A running watcher holds a lock on <data>/watcher.lock. watch stop and watch status report "not running" (and remove watcher.pid) when no process holds it, instead of trusting the PID in watcher.pid: a PID file left by a dead watcher no longer gets an unrelated process (one that reused the PID) killed. watch start refuses while the lock is held.

    wayu doctor checks#

    • The turbo export check looks for turbo.<ext> of the current shell (turbo.bash for bash): a bash setup sourcing turbo.bash was reported as "sources turbo.zsh but it is not generated" (error, exit 78).
    • The plugins check parses plugins.json with the same strict reader as wayu plugin list: a malformed file, an invalid value or a dependency cycle is an error (exit 78; it was "✓ N plugin(s) installed", exit 0). The cycle explanation goes to stderr, so doctor --json stays valid JSON.
    • The shell configuration check sees startup lines that load wayu through builtin source, command source / command . or zsh-defer source (they were "wayu not sourced", exit 78).
    • With no startup file at all, the shell configuration warning names the file to create and the source line to put in it (it said "run 'wayu init'", which never creates one).
    • wayu init prints its "Created N config file(s)" summary after the last file and counts all of them (it said 3 after five "Created" lines). The TUI settings view has a "Data dir" row.

    search and secret display#

    • wayu search matches names only (PATH entries: key or directory): alias commands are no longer searched (a token inside one was findable, like constant values before 6.0.0). --json field is always name, and an encrypted constant has "secret": true (text: ********).
    • wayu search matches a PATH entry by its key as well as its directory (one result per entry, showing the directory).
    • const list --json: an encrypted constant's source is wayu (secret) / wayu (secret, inactive), as in the text view (was wayu / wayu (inactive)).

    CLI flags and arguments#

    • The hidden wayu completions list --generate / -g spelling is gone (exit 64; wayu completions --generate never worked): use wayu completions generate.
    • Flags and words that meant nothing exit 64 instead of being ignored: --full / -f / --source outside path|alias|const list (and --tui), --test / --snapshot without -c=, doctor --profile with --json or --fix, two export modes (export --eval --check), and an extra word after an action that takes none (path list x, secrets lock x, toml validate x, plugin list x, ...).
    • -c=<component> is the developer component flag only before a command word: wayu plugin search -c=dev no longer runs the component tester (it exits 64 as an unknown option; use --category dev / -c dev).

    Backups, plugins, scripts and functions#

    • Backups of files in a subdirectory of the config/data dir (functions, scripts) are named after their path relative to that dir: @functions%init.zsh.backup.<stamp>, shown as functions/init.zsh by backup list (was the bare file name, so functions/init.zsh shared — and pruned — the history of init.zsh, and functions/extra.zsh that of extra.zsh). Existing backups of such files keep their old name and group.
    • plugins.json backups are pruned to the newest 5 like every other file's (every plugin command added one, never removed). A plugin command whose backup fails now writes nothing and exits with an error (was a warning).
    • plugins.json with an entry without a name, two entries with the same name, or a use glob containing / ("../../etc/*") is invalid: every command that reads it exits 78 naming the entry. Fix the entry by hand.
    • plugin update --all counts only plugins whose checkout moved as "updated" and reports the rest as "N already up to date" (all fetched plugins were counted as updated).
    • TUI plugins view (Installed tab): u updates the selected plugin (Esc cancels), d removes it after a confirmation (was a hint to use the CLI).
    • wayu script: a source in any language can declare its build command in a header comment (// wayu: build = cc -O2 -o {out} {src}); swift's swiftc -O is now a preset of the same mechanism. The build hash covers the build command too, so every swift script is rebuilt once.
    • Two script sources with the same name (foo.sh, foo.rb) are an error: neither is built (script build exits 1, they used to replace each other's bin/foo on every build), script edit|build|rm foo exit 65 and doctor reports an error. Delete or rename one.
    • A script whose shebang line ends in CR (CRLF line endings) is not linked (script build exits 1 explaining it) and doctor reports an error; script import converts such a file to LF (it was imported and failed with bad interpreter).
    • script rm NAME --yes removes a bin/NAME entry that has no script (was exit 65); doctor reports those entries as a separate, fixable check ("script bin entries", was part of "scripts") and doctor --fix --yes removes them.
    • Shebangs #!/usr/bin/env -u VAR python / -P dir / -C dir / --unset=VAR are read correctly (the option's argument was taken as the interpreter); #!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script (PEP 723) is a python script.

    Security hardening (audit)#

    Files and directories:

    • wayu's config and data dirs (and functions/, scripts/, bin/, backup/, run/) are created 0700 whatever the umask; wayu init tightens existing ones (they hold startup code, and bin/ is on PATH). wayu doctor reports a group/other-writable wayu dir as an error (exit 78, new "directory permissions" check); doctor --fix --yes tightens it.
    • config extend creates extra.<ext> 0600; new function files are 0600.
    • <data>/backup must be a real directory you own: a symlink there is refused (commands that back up first fail with an I/O error); symlinks inside it are not listed or restored, and a secrets.json copy is restored only when it is a regular file.
    • script new exits 65 when the path is a symlink; script import skips one; function add exits 73 on a dangling symlink.

    Secrets:

    • The keystore tools are never looked up in PATH: macOS uses /usr/bin/security; secret-tool is taken from /usr/bin, /usr/local/bin, /bin or /run/current-system/sw/bin (not found: backend = "auto" falls back to file, "secret-service" errors). The master key is no longer passed on a command line.
    • secrets.json with a duplicate key or nesting deeper than 64 is invalid (exit 78).
    • A session cache dir with group/other permission bits is not used (the cache goes to <data>/run/wayu-<uid>/). The loader in core.<ext> changed: run wayu build once. bash/fish startup with secrets runs one ls -ldn to check the dir.
    • secrets lock and every secret change delete the session cache in every dir wayu wrote one to (listed in <data>/run/cache-dirs).
    • const add NAME VALUE --secret / --run-only warns on stderr that the value is visible in ps and shell history: omit VALUE (prompted) or pipe it on stdin.
    • wayu optimize masks secret-looking lines in its diff, and after moving a secret warns that the rc backup (used by undo) still holds it in plain text.

    Generated shell code (run wayu build once):

    • Native prompt: the pending-changes count runs git with core.fsmonitor off and skips submodule contents, and is not shown in a repo whose own config defines filter.<x>.clean / .process (a cloned repo could run code from the prompt). Global/system filters (git-lfs) still count.
    • fish: aliases are functions that run their body through eval (alias still lists them); an invalid body fails when used, not at startup.
    • Constants: ${X=v} / ${X:=v} in a value stay literal (they assigned in the shell at startup); use ${X:-v}.
    • wayu export --eval output is only supported quoted: eval "$(wayu export --eval)".
    • [tools] keys that are not valid command names are skipped with a warning for every kind.

    Names and values:

    • More protected constant names (exit 65): PS0-PS4, PROMPT, prompt, PROMPT2-PROMPT4, RPROMPT, RPROMPT2, RPS1, RPS2, SPROMPT, PROMPT_EOL_MARK, PROMPT_COMMAND, BASH_ENV, ENV, fish_function_path, fish_complete_path. Stored ones are no longer exported; wayu doctor reports them; wayu const rm NAME removes them.
    • Alias names starting with _wayu are refused (exit 65); a stored one is a config error (exit 78).
    • fpath entries with glob characters (* ? [ ] ( ) < > | # ^ ~, except a leading ~) are a config error (exit 78); completions fpath add refuses them (exit 65) and optimize leaves such an rc line in place.
    • wayu.toml strings with raw control characters (below 0x20 except tab, and DEL; multi-line strings may span lines) are invalid for validate, doctor and backup restore: use escapes. Nesting deeper than 128 is a parse error. toml validate/keys/doctor print control characters in key and table names as \xHH.
    • plugins.json: installed_path must be directly inside <data>/plugins (else exit 78 naming the file); refs must be valid git ref names; control characters in names and nesting deeper than 64 are refused.
    • hooks.conf: a placeholder inside "…" within '…' is invalid (exit 78): write it unquoted inside '…' or use "$WAYU_HOOK_NAME".

    Output:

    • Human-readable output shows control characters from your data escaped instead of sending them to the terminal (a stored value could set the title, clear the screen or write the clipboard): path/alias/const list, plugin list/get/search, script list, search and doctor print tab as \t, newline as \n, other C0 controls, DEL and invalid UTF-8 bytes as \xHH, C1 controls as \u00HH. const list used to drop ESC[... sequences and turn newlines into spaces; it now shows them escaped like the other lists. --json and get output are unchanged (exact values). The TUI shows them escaped in lists and as � elsewhere.
    • Developer component flags: -c=<component> width= / height= outside 1-1000 exit 64.

    Commands:

    • Plugin git commands never run a checkout's core.fsmonitor or hooks.
    • script import of a file whose wayu: build = header is not a preset needs --allow-build (else exit 64, nothing imported); --dry-run and the summary show the command. Script build commands run in <data>/scripts.
    • Ctrl-C / SIGTERM / SIGHUP while wayu runs git, a compiler or a shell kills that process group, removes a partial plugin clone and exits 130 / 143 / 129.
    • wayu optimize / auto_optimize read quotes inside $(...) and ${...}; a comment, case or heredoc inside $(...), or a ' inside "${...}", keeps that line and everything after it in the rc file.
    • wayu doctor no longer runs rc generator commands to time them (see above); the startup estimate covers compinit only.
    • watch stop exits 1 without signalling when watcher.pid does not name the process holding the watcher lock.
    • Release builds: the Odin toolchain download is checked against .github/odin-release.sha256; release archives are reproducible and attested.

    6.0.0#

    PATH entries, aliases and constants move to entries.json; data dir is ~/.local/share/wayu#

    • The default data dir is now ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/wayu (was: the config dir). It holds init.<ext>, the generated files, plugins.json, plugins/, completions/, backup/ and the lock. WAYU_DATA_DIR still overrides it, and no longer follows WAYU_CONFIG_DIR. wayu init creates both dirs.
    • The rc line is now source "${WAYU_DATA_DIR:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/wayu}/init.zsh" (init.bash likewise; fish: see the README). Replace the old source "$HOME/.config/wayu/init.zsh" line; wayu init prints the new one.
    • [paths], [aliases] and [env] are no longer read from wayu.toml. They live in <data>/entries.json ({"version":1,"paths":[{"key","dir"}],"aliases":[{"name","value"}],"env":[{"name","value"}]}), written only by wayu (wayu path|alias|const, the TUI, templates): atomic, owner-only (0600), pretty-printed, stable order. A malformed entries.json makes every command that reads it exit 78 naming the file; a missing one is empty.
    • Nothing is converted. To upgrade: run wayu init, re-add each entry with wayu path add <key>=<dir>, wayu alias add <name> <command> and wayu const add <NAME> <value> (in the old file order), delete the three tables from wayu.toml, move plugins.json and plugins/ from ~/.config/wayu to the data dir (or re-add the plugins), and update the rc line. wayu toml validate (exit 65) and wayu doctor (exit 78) report a leftover [paths] / [aliases] / [env] table with the command to use.
    • wayu toml show prints wayu.toml verbatim; --reveal is gone (exit 64).
    • wayu backup: types are toml (wayu.toml) and entries (entries.json; path, alias and constants name it too). A restore of entries reverts all PATH entries, aliases and constants.
    • wayu doctor has an entries check (error when entries.json does not parse).
    • plugin list --json conflicts: with is "entries.json" (was "wayu.toml") for a clash with your aliases / constants.
    • Messages: path add prints Added to PATH: <dir>, a missing entry is PATH entry not found: <dir>, alias add prints Alias added: <name>, dry runs print Would update entries.json (aliases) etc.

    Notes further down this section that describe [paths], [aliases] or [env] in wayu.toml (editing, reading, toml show masking) now apply to the same entries in entries.json, or no longer apply.

    Functions move to the data dir; new wayu script#

    • functions/ now lives in the data dir ($WAYU_DATA_DIR/functions), not the config dir: wayu function writes there, core.<ext> sources only that dir, and wayu init creates it there. Nothing is moved for you: mv ~/.config/wayu/functions/* "${WAYU_DATA_DIR:-${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/wayu}/functions/".
    • New wayu script (scripts): standalone executables in any language (swift compiled with swiftc; python, ruby, node, bun, bash, zsh, fish, perl, lua, sh linked) in <data>/scripts/, run from <data>/bin/. wayu init creates both dirs. Once bin/ holds a script, core.<ext> / path_sync.<ext> put it first among wayu's PATH entries (zsh, bash, fish), so a script can shadow a tool of the same name; wayu export --eval includes it too.
    • wayu build and wayu reload rebuild stale scripts; wayu doctor has a scripts check (stale or broken scripts, bin/ entries without a script). New exit code 69 (EXIT_UNAVAILABLE): script new when the language's interpreter or compiler is not on PATH.
    • wayu.toml accepts [scripts] default_lang; an unknown language is a toml validate error (exit 65).

    Encrypted secrets (const add --secret, wayu secrets, [secrets])#

    • wayu const add NAME [VALUE] --secret stores the value encrypted (ChaCha20-Poly1305) in <data>/secrets.json; the master key lives in the macOS keychain / Secret Service / <config>/secret.key ([secrets] backend). Without VALUE it is read from stdin. const get decrypts, const rm removes, const list shows ******** with source wayu (secret); in --json such a row is {"constant", "secret": true, "source"} with no value.
    • Converting a plain constant with --secret deletes the entries.json backups that still hold its plaintext value.
    • A --secret at the end of a const add line is now a flag, not part of the value (like --dry-run). To store the literal text, put -- before the value. --secret anywhere else exits 64.
    • A plain const add of a name that is a secret exits 65.
    • New wayu secrets list|rekey|lock. [secrets] is a known wayu.toml table; an unknown backend makes toml validate exit 65.
    • When secrets exist, core.<ext>, turbo.<ext> and export --eval get a Secrets section after the constants that sources a per-session cache in ${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-${TMPDIR:-/tmp}}/wayu-<uid>/ (running wayu secrets cache once when it is stale). Nothing changes for configs without secrets.
    • wayu doctor has a secrets check (an info row when there are none); its message counts run-only secrets.
    • Run-only secrets: wayu const add NAME [VALUE] --run-only (implies --secret) stores a secret that is never exported to shells (not in the session cache, core, turbo or export --eval). const list shows it with source wayu (run-only), --json adds "run_only": true. Re-adding with --secret / --run-only switches the mode.
    • New wayu secrets run NAME... -- CMD [ARGS...]: execs CMD (PATH lookup, no shell) with those secrets added to the environment. Exit 64 without --/names/CMD, 65 for an unknown name, 127 / 126 when CMD is not found / not executable; otherwise CMD's own status.
    • wayu secrets list prints a mode column (session / run-only) after each name.

    wayu build eval removed; zsh PATH order restored after login#

    • wayu build eval is gone (exit 64). It rebuilt every generated file at each shell start, which nothing needs: every wayu write regenerates them and the prompt hook runs wayu build when wayu.toml or entries.json was edited by hand. Replace eval "$(wayu build eval)" in rc files with the source line above (or init.bash). eval "$(wayu export --eval)" (env/PATH/aliases only) is unchanged.
    • zsh: at the first prompt wayu puts its PATH entries' dirs back in front of the dirs that were on PATH when it loaded or that macOS path_helper manages (/etc/paths, /etc/paths.d). Loading wayu from ~/.zshenv therefore keeps wayu's PATH precedence in login shells; dirs prepended in .zshrc stay ahead.
    • zsh native prompt: PROMPT/RPROMPT are set again at the first prompt, so /etc/zshrc (macOS sets PS1) or .zshrc can't replace them when wayu is loaded from .zshenv. To manage the prompt yourself, set [prompt] enabled = false.

    Removed: backward compatibility#

    wayu now reads only the current formats: wayu.toml, entries.json, plugins.json, hooks.conf, functions/<name>.<ext>, extra.<ext> and the files the current generator writes. Configs left by older releases are not converted or tolerated any more. Upgrade from the previous release only.

    • wayu migrate (legacy shell files → wayu.toml, --schema, --from/--to) and wayu toml convert are removed (exit 64). Use wayu --shell <shell> init to set up another shell. wayu build without a wayu.toml exits 78.
    • The 3.x [[paths]] / [[aliases]] / [[constants]] schema is no longer detected: no exit 78 with a migration hint, no backup-restore refusal. toml validate rejects it (exit 65) and doctor reports an error.
    • path.<ext>, aliases.<ext> and constants.<ext> are neither created by wayu init nor read: init.<ext> sources only core.<ext> (and prints a wayu build hint when it is missing), core.<ext> no longer sources path.<ext>, wayu watch no longer watches them, and the TUI/search read wayu.toml only.
    • Only an untouched init.<ext> from the previous release is refreshed; an older one is treated as edited (kept, with a warning): move it aside and run wayu init. Leftover lazy, login and helpers.<ext> files are no longer deleted.
    • plugins.conf is ignored (no migration to plugins.json). Enum values in plugins.json must be names ("zsh", "source"); numbers fail to load (exit 78). The unused entry_file and profiles fields are no longer written.
    • Backups are listed, restored and pruned only under the current name (<file>.backup.YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS.UUUUUU[-N]); older names are ignored. A backup dir left group/world-readable by an old release is no longer tightened (new backups are still 0600 in a 0700 dir).
    • Keys wayu never read are no longer parsed: wayu_version, [settings] auto_backup / fuzzy_fallback / dry_run_default, [path] dedup / clean, [[plugins]], [profile.*], [prompt.username] style_user, [prompt.interactive] async_interval. toml validate prints a warning per unknown key or table, with its line, and still exits 0; a known table in the wrong shape ([[paths]], paths = …) is an error (exit 65). doctor warns about unknown keys.
    • A top-level shell = "…" in wayu.toml is not read; use [shell] type.
    • functions/: zsh sources only *.zsh, bash only *.bash (fish already *.fish); files without that extension are no longer sourced. Functions under the old ~/.local/share/wayu/functions are no longer copied over.

    Notes further down this section about wayu migrate, the [[paths]] refusal, plugins.conf or the legacy shell files describe changes made before these features were removed; they no longer apply.

    Unknown actions, wayu toml#

    • wayu toml with no action validates wayu.toml (same as toml validate, as its help always said); it printed a fixed key list.
    • wayu toml keys lists wayu.toml's real top-level keys and tables in file order; it printed a fixed shell path aliases constants plugins hooks. A file that doesn't parse exits 65.
    • An action word a command doesn't have exits 64 with that command's help for toml, hooks, config, template and function too (they showed help or the hook list and exited 0). doctor with a non-flag argument exits 64; doctor help shows its help.
    • --source other than wayu|external|inactive|all and --shell other than zsh|bash|fish exit 64; they were silently accepted (an unknown --source listed nothing, an unknown --shell kept the detected shell).
    • plugin add help / plugin add --help show the add help instead of looking up a plugin named help (exit 65).
    • alias / const usage errors and help name the real command (wayu alias add, wayu const add; alias said wayu aliases, which is not a command), and no longer list argument-less forms such as wayu alias add (the CLI never prompts).

    Alias names may contain -#

    • wayu alias add, toml validate and the TUI now accept a hyphen in an alias name after the first character (onlead-logs). zsh, bash and fish all accept these names and TOML writes them as bare keys. A leading - is still refused, as are hyphens in constant and function names. Configs that toml validate used to reject for this reason now pass.

    Hooks#

    • A {path} / {name} / {value} placeholder inside double quotes in hooks.conf is now refused. The shell expanded the value before a nested sh -c "..." / eval "..." re-parsed it, so pre_alias_add = sh -c "echo {value}" ran code from an alias value. Such a hook never runs: any wayu operation that would run hooks exits 78 before writing anything and names the offending hooks.conf line; wayu hooks marks it INVALID. Write the placeholder unquoted (echo Adding {path}, wayu quotes the value), inside '...' for an inner shell (sh -c 'echo {path}'), or use "$WAYU_HOOK_PATH" / "$WAYU_HOOK_NAME" / "$WAYU_HOOK_VALUE" when you need double quotes. (This replaces the 4.4.x advice to use double quotes for direct substitution.)

    Secret values in list views#

    • const list (text and --json, with and without --full) now shows secret-looking values (names with KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASS, API, AUTH, …, or token-shaped values) as ******** — both wayu.toml [env] entries and external environment variables. Scripts that read values from const list --json must add --reveal, or use const get NAME (unchanged, prints the real value). The text table ends with a hint when something was masked.
    • toml show masks secret-looking [env] values the same way; toml show --reveal prints the file verbatim.
    • --reveal is accepted only by const and toml; elsewhere it is an unknown option (exit 64).
    • TUI constants view: values are masked by default; v toggles reveal (the footer shows v Reveal / v Hide) and resets when you leave the view. The / filter matches the masked text, so typing part of a secret no longer finds its row. The detail overlay (Enter) follows the same toggle.

    Plugins (review fixes)#

    • plugin update|enable|disable|priority|get|rm NAME match the exact plugin name (or display name) only, like const get. A miss prints nothing on stdout, lists up to 5 similar plugin names on stderr and exits 65; it never acts on a fuzzy guess (plugin disable rig used to disable origin) and never prompts. plugin rm of an unknown name now exits 65 too (it exited 0 "already removed" when nothing was similar).
    • plugin update no longer resets a checkout whose HEAD has commits that were never on the remote: when it cannot fast-forward, the update fails (exit 74) instead of discarding those commits. Push/rebase them or reinstall the plugin.
    • plugins.json dependencies entries must be valid plugin names (no newline, /, leading -, empty, ./..); otherwise any command that reads it exits 78. A newline in one used to inject shell code into the generated plugins.<ext>.

    build profile#

    • The phase breakdown inlines plugins.<ext>: it has a row per [tools] entry (tool <name> (evalcache), tool nvm (lazy), tool <name> (lazy)) and per plugin (plugin <name>) instead of one Tools / Plugins row; core sections keep their names. Rows with no code are left out.
    • bash: the breakdown now runs too when the shell has $EPOCHREALTIME (bash 5+); with an older bash it prints a note instead.

    Plugin conflicts#

    • A function, alias or exported variable defined by two enabled plugins, or by a plugin and your wayu.toml ([aliases] / [env]), is now reported: plugin add and plugin enable print a warning (stderr) naming each one, plugin list ends with a conflicts section (stderr), plugin list --json has a "conflicts": [{"kind", "name", "with"}] array per plugin (with is a plugin name or "wayu.toml"), and wayu doctor adds a plugin conflicts warning (exit code unchanged). Several statements on one line (export X=1; alias gs=...) are all scanned; the ones after the first were ignored.

    Plugins: installing and loading#

    • plugin add (and TUI install) refuses a repository with nothing to load for the plugin's shell(s): it exits 65, removes the fresh clone and writes nothing (it used to report success while the loader sourced nothing). Name the entry file with the new repeatable plugin add <url> --use <file-or-glob> (matched at the repository root; stored as use in plugins.json). Any other extra argument to plugin add is now an error (exit 64).
    • plugin add <url> records the shells the repository actually has files for (ZSH, BASH, BOTH, FISH or ANY) instead of always BOTH, so a fish-only plugin added by URL now loads in fish, and a zsh-only one is listed as zsh.
    • Generated plugins.<ext>: only the FIRST existing root entry file is sourced (<name>.plugin.<ext>, <name>.<ext>, <name>-init.<ext>, init.<ext>, plugin.<ext>); plugins that ship both <name>.plugin.zsh and <name>.zsh were loaded twice. New entry files: <name>.zsh-theme (zsh; e.g. powerlevel10k), <name>.plugin.sh / <name>.sh (zsh and bash; e.g. rupa/z), and a top-level *.zsh-theme when there is no *.zsh. Takes effect the next time the loader is regenerated (any plugin change, wayu init).
    • Registry: entries whose repository has no shell entry file were removed — binary tools (starship, zoxide, atuin, fzf, ripgrep, bat, eza, delta, direnv, mise, volta, rustup, oh-my-posh, asdf, pyenv, rbenv), autojump, fasd, git-extras, git-flow, plus zsh-history-enquirer (pointed at zsh-command-time) and zsh-dotenv (not a cloneable URL). plugin add <key> for them exits 65; install the tool with your package manager and load it from wayu.toml [tools] (e.g. zoxide = { kind = "evalcache", args = "init zsh" }). Already-installed plugins are unaffected.
    • pure-fish now installs as pure-fish (it shared the name pure with the zsh prompt). An existing fish pure install keeps its name.

    Plugins: network git#

    • Clone, fetch and ls-remote run without a terminal and with deadlines: ssh runs as ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 (unless you set GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_SSH or core.sshCommand), so a host-key or passphrase prompt fails instead of hanging or garbling the TUI — load the key into ssh-agent / accept the host key first. https transfers below 1000 B/s for 30 s abort (GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT/_TIME override). Each command is killed after 10 min (clone/fetch) or 60 s (plugin check); WAYU_GIT_TIMEOUT=<seconds> changes both.
    • A failed plugin add clone now prints git's error.

    Building from source#

    • ./build_it install installs to $PREFIX/bin (default ~/.local/bin, was /usr/local/bin), replaces the binary atomically (temp file + rename), refuses while Homebrew manages wayu (--force to override), and warns when another wayu shadows the installed one on PATH.

    path#

    • path clean resolves $VAR/${VAR} from wayu.toml [env] first, then the environment (as the generated init does), and never removes an entry whose variable is set in neither. path dedup also resolves [env] variables, so $TOOLS/bin and its absolute form count as duplicates.
    • path clean/path dedup exit 78 without changing anything when a dropped entry shares its key with a kept one (hand-edited duplicate key in [paths]); they used to delete both lines.
    • pre_path_remove/post_path_remove hooks get the entry's directory as {path} when path rm is given a key (they got the key).

    [env] values (generated core.zsh / core.bash / core.fish)#

    • Only named variables expand: $NAME, ${NAME} and ${NAME...} / ${#NAME} with a closing } (zsh/bash; e.g. ${X:-default}). Every other $ is now literal: $1, $$, $?, a trailing $, $%, an unclosed ${ (was a syntax error that dropped the whole core file) and zsh flags like ${(e)...} (which evaluated the text, running commands).
    • zsh: $NAME is emitted as ${NAME}, so $HOME:h… / $HOME[1] are no longer zsh modifiers/subscripts — zsh now gives the same value as bash.
    • fish: ${NAME}, a bare $ or $$ no longer make core.fish fail to parse (fish then loaded none of wayu's env, PATH or aliases). ${NAME:-x} has no fish equivalent and is kept literal in fish.
    • zsh/bash: ${NAME<op>...} expands only with - = + ? (each also with a leading :), #, % or / (e.g. ${X:-d}, ${X#pre}, ${X/a/b}); ${#NAME} only without an operator. Everything else is now literal, e.g. ${X@P} (bash ≥ 4.4 ran a $(...) stored in X), ${X[Y]} / ${X:Y} (bash evaluated Y arithmetically, running a $(...) hidden in Y's value), ${X: -2}, ${X^} and zsh modifiers such as ${HOME:h} (zsh aborted core.zsh on an unknown modifier).
    • fish: $NAME followed by a non-ASCII letter ($HOMEé) no longer reads as the longer variable name HOMEé.

    functions/#

    • fish now sources functions/*.fish (core.fish never loaded them).
    • zsh no longer sources functions/*.bash / *.fish, bash no longer sources functions/*.zsh / *.fish (other shells' files from wayu function add were parse errors at every startup). Files without those extensions are still sourced by zsh and bash.

    Completions (zsh)#

    • core.zsh also rebuilds .zcompdump when the list of files in the completions dir changed, so a completion added in the same second as the dump is no longer missed. The list seen at the last rebuild is kept in ${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zcompdump.wayu; the first shell after upgrading rebuilds the dump once.

    Completions for wayu itself (zsh, bash, fish)#

    • The first argument of path|alias|const rm|get, plugin rm|get|enable|disable|priority|update, function add|edit|rm and completions rm completes existing entries (paths as written in wayu.toml, alias/constant/plugin/function/completion names). The scripts list them by running the hidden wayu completions names <kind> ($_WAYU_BIN, else wayu on PATH) at TAB time. Re-run wayu completions generate to update installed scripts.
    • fish: action words are offered only right after the command (wayu alias rm <TAB> no longer offers add, list, …); flags still complete anywhere.

    migrate --schema#

    • Values it can't convert exactly (multi-line """ strings, arrays, inline tables) in the rewritten sections are listed as wayu.toml:N; nothing is written and it exits 65. They used to be dropped silently (an alias with a """ command became ""). A section header with a trailing comment ([aliases] # mine) is now recognised.
    • Waits for other wayu commands (config lock) before rewriting wayu.toml.
    • [[paths]] / [[aliases]] / [[constants]] fields the modern schema has no place for (legacy description, export, secret, …) are listed on stderr as wayu.toml:N warnings; they used to vanish silently. The migration still runs (exit 0).

    doctor#

    • A relative [paths] entry (./node_modules/.bin) is no longer reported as missing or removed by doctor --fix: it is counted with the entries that "use unset variables or relative paths (left alone)".
    • doctor --fix exits 78 and changes nothing when a key it would drop is repeated in [paths] (a = "/x" twice); it used to delete every line of that key, the kept entry included.
    • bash: new warning bash PROMPT_COMMAND when a bash startup file replaces PROMPT_COMMAND after the line that loads wayu (it dropped the _wayu_paths_sync hook, so open shells missed wayu path add/rm). Shown only when such a line exists; exit status unchanged (warnings never exit 78).
    • shell configuration / Sync status: only a line that runs source, . or eval counts as loading wayu; a line that just mentions the file (alias e='vim ~/.config/wayu/init.zsh') no longer passes.
    • Sync status now compares the [paths] entries with the $PATH doctor runs in: OK when all are present, INFO "N of M PATH entries not in this shell's $PATH" otherwise (it used to claim "All wayu entries are loaded" from the rc text alone).
    • A [paths] entry using an environment variable whose value is relative ($FOO/bin with FOO=rel) counts as unresolved, never missing.
    • backups: a missing backup directory (fresh install) is INFO "No backups yet", not a warning.
    • Dependencies: checks git plus the configured shell (zsh, bash or fish) instead of always zsh.

    Backups#

    • wayu backup restore waits for other wayu commands (config lock) instead of racing them; a concurrent edit can no longer overwrite the restore.

    • Backup times are UTC and now say so: backup list prints 2026-11-07 14:35:37 UTC; backup list --json timestamp is ISO-8601 (2026-11-07T14:35:37Z, was 2026-11-07 14:35:37).

    • backup list and backup rm (no type) cover every file in the backup directory, not only wayu.toml: the rc file wayu init edits, init.zsh (--optimize), plugins.json, ... Each --json group's file is the wayu file name or the rc path (~/.config/zsh/.zshrc). backup restore still restores wayu.toml only; copy other backups back by hand.

    • Backups of files outside wayu's directories are named after their path relative to $HOME with / as % (.config%zsh%.zshrc.backup.*), so ~/.zshrc and $ZDOTDIR/.zshrc keep separate histories (~/.zshrc keeps the old .zshrc.backup.* name).

    • Backups were silently skipped when the config path contained .backup. (HOME=/x/my.backup.d); only the file name is checked now.

    • backup restore prunes to the 5 newest backups after its pre-restore snapshot (never the backup it restored), so repeated restores no longer grow the directory.

    • backup restore <type> N: N must be decimal digits; 0x1 / +1 are treated as file names (exit 65), not #1.

    • wayu backup list|restore|rm work while wayu.toml still uses the obsolete [[paths]] schema (they exited 78).

    • backup restore refuses a wayu.toml backup that uses the obsolete [[paths]] / [[aliases]] / [[constants]] schema (exit 74, file unchanged); restoring one made every other command exit 78, including the undo backup restore <type> 1. Copy such a backup over wayu.toml by hand and run wayu migrate --schema.

    init.<ext> from wayu ≤ 3.9#

    • An unmodified init.zsh written by wayu 3.9 or older is now recognised and updated to the current template (old file backed up), like newer ones. It used to be kept with a "has local edits" warning, so after wayu migrate it still sourced the emptied legacy files and the shell got no PATH, aliases or constants.

    TUI#

    • Adding or deleting an entry while wayu.toml uses the obsolete [[paths]] schema (e.g. replaced by an old wayu after the TUI started) is refused with "run wayu migrate --schema"; it used to append a [paths] table to the old-schema file.
    • The Backups view lists wayu.toml backups and Settings counts them; both only looked at the pre-3.10 path/aliases/constants files, so they showed none.
    • Adding in the TUI follows wayu path add / alias add / const add: PATH input name=path sets the [paths] key (it was stored as a path relative to the TUI's directory), and the path must resolve and exist (relative paths resolve against the directory wayu was started in); otherwise the form shows the CLI's reason. Adding an alias or constant that already exists asks "REPLACE …?" first. Notifications say Added / Updated / Already present, nothing changed (a duplicate PATH said Added).
    • --dry-run: a DRY RUN badge sits on the top border; previews read [dry-run] would add alias: x = "…" / [dry-run] would remove … (were Dry run: would …). Plugin enable/disable/install no longer write plugins.json under --dry-run (install recorded a plugin that was never cloned).
    • Keys: r / Ctrl+R / F5 reload every view; views also reload by themselves when wayu.toml, plugins.json, hooks.conf or the backup directory change on disk. e edits the selected entry (a PATH keeps its key and position; a renamed alias/constant replaces the old name; secret values must be revealed with v first). u restores the newest wayu.toml backup after a confirmation. Text fields edit at a cursor (←/→, Home/End, Ctrl+A/E/U/K/W, Delete) and show the end of long input.
    • Plugins: Enter shows details on both tabs (on Registry it used to install at once); i installs after a confirmation; on Installed, space toggles enabled, e enables, x disables, and d (which disabled) only shows the wayu plugin rm command.
    • Backups view lists every backup group (plugins.json, the rc file, init files…, newest first). Enter on a wayu.toml backup restores it after a confirmation (like wayu backup restore); c asks, then prunes every group to the newest 5 (it targeted pre-3.10 files and removed nothing).
    • Long operations show a progress frame and can be cancelled with Esc / Ctrl+C: the alias view's $SHELL -i -c alias (now given up after 3 s, listing no external aliases), plugin clones, and hooks (in the TUI a hook is stopped after 30 s).
    • Hooks view lists every hook event with its command; space disables a hook by commenting its hooks.conf line as # disabled: <line> (and enables it again), t runs it once with sample values and shows its output.
    • Settings view: Enter toggles dry-run or colors for the session (nothing is saved); also shows the editor and the backups kept per file.
    • Below 40x12 the TUI shows "Terminal too small" instead of an empty layout. It quits when its terminal input is closed (EOF) instead of spinning.

    wayu.toml parsing (one parser for every command)#

    • toml validate, doctor, backup restore, migrate --schema, the TUI, alias/const/path list, the shell generator and the in-place editor now share one TOML parser, so they agree on every file.
    • Now accepted as valid (were "Failed to parse" for toml validate, the TUI and doctor): a UTF-8 BOM, arrays spanning several lines (e.g. [settings] autosuggestions_accept_keys), quoted keys (".." = "cd .."), dotted keys, floats and dates.
    • Now rejected by toml validate / doctor / backup restore: a key defined twice in one table, a table defined twice, integers with leading zeros. Other commands keep working on such a file as before.
    • toml validate and doctor name the offending line: Failed to parse <file>: line 5: invalid value "ls" (strings must be quoted).
    • Quoted keys are decoded everywhere: "q\"k" = … is the alias q"k in alias list (was listed with its quotes) and alias rm .. finds ".." = … (said "not found").
    • TUI: [paths] are shown in file order (= PATH priority; were sorted by key), and entries of a file with a syntax error are shown like alias list shows them (the view was empty).
    • [paths]/[aliases]/[env]: arrays and inline tables are skipped (the raw text, e.g. ["a"], used to be exported). Integers are read as their value (N = 1_000 → 1000). A key containing a dot written bare (g.st = …, which wayu itself wrote for such alias names) is still the name g.st.
    • wayu writes keys that need it quoted ("g.st" = "git status") and escapes control characters in values (\u001B), so everything it writes is valid TOML.
    • migrate --schema lists (instead of copying verbatim) lines that are not valid TOML, such as an unquoted value.
    • An edit refused because a table holds a broken multi-line value now says why (wayu.toml line N: unterminated array (missing ']') in [env] …).
    • [shell] type is written lowercase ("zsh", "bash", "fish"; was "ZSH", "Bash", "Fish", "Unknown") by wayu init, migrate --from X --to Y and any command that creates a missing wayu.toml. wayu config edit on a missing file creates the same scaffold (it wrote [settings] shell = "zsh" plus commented examples), and so does legacy wayu migrate (it started the file with a comment line and no [shell]).
    • toml validate now checks [shell] type (case-insensitive); it only saw a top-level shell = … key before. A value other than zsh/bash/fish — including "Unknown", written when no shell was detected — fails with Invalid shell: unknown (must be zsh, bash, or fish).

    WAYU_CONFIG_DIR / WAYU_DATA_DIR#

    • WAYU_DATA_DIR is honoured when WAYU_CONFIG_DIR is also set (it was ignored: data always went to the config dir). Data dir = WAYU_DATA_DIR, else the config dir.
    • init.zsh / init.bash / init.fish find their files next to themselves instead of in ~/.config/wayu, so the rc line works without exporting the overrides to the shell (it used to fail with "no such file" and load no PATH/aliases). The config dir falls back to the init file's dir when that holds wayu.toml. An unmodified init file is updated on the next regeneration (backup first).
    • When the dirs differ from the defaults, core.<ext> exports WAYU_CONFIG_DIR / WAYU_DATA_DIR, so wayu commands typed in that shell (and the path-sync background wayu build) use the same dirs.

    [tools] evalcache#

    • The cache is regenerated when the tool's binary changes, not only when it gets newer: zsh compares resolved path + size + mtime + inode, bash the path, the exact mtime and the inode/resolved target. Cache files now start with a # wayu-evalcache: line; old caches are rebuilt once. bash also keeps a <cache>.bin link next to each cache file.
    • The tool is looked up in PATH only and run as command <tool> (a function or alias of that name is no longer called).
    • New wayu build clean deletes the cache (${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-~/.cache}/wayu/evalcache), for init output that depends on config or environment.
    • args is split into words like the shell does (quotes honoured) and each word is quoted in the generated call; $NAME / ${NAME...} and a leading ~/ still expand, {a,b} no longer brace-expands. Args containing a newline, ; & | < > ( ), $(...) / backticks or glob characters (* ? [) are refused: wayu build exits 78 naming the tool, other regenerations skip the tool with a warning on stderr.

    Prompt (zsh, [prompt] enabled = true)#

    • Default modules have separators like starship: {username}{dir}{git_branch}{character} with [$user](white bold) in , [$dir](cyan bold) and on [$branch](magenta bold) . Custom format / module formats are unchanged.
    • The user name shows only over SSH or as root unless [prompt.username] show_always = true (the setting was ignored).
    • vi mode is opt-in: the prompt no longer switches the line editor to the vi keymap or sets KEYTIMEOUT. vi users: add vi_mode = true under [prompt] to get bindkey -v, KEYTIMEOUT=1 (no longer exported to child processes) and the mode indicator ([prompt.interactive] vi_mode_indicator = false keeps the keymap without the indicator). Without vi mode the {character} module shows success/error by exit status.
    • zle-line-init / zle-keymap-select are chained: a widget already installed under that name (yours, a plugin's, another prompt's) is kept as _wayu_prev_<name> and runs first; it used to be replaced.
    • The git branch is read without running git (walks up to .git, reads HEAD; worktrees/submodules and $GIT_DIR included; detached HEAD shows the first 7 characters of the commit id) — two git processes per prompt are gone. The dirty count is still fetched asynchronously.
    • The prompt toggle is off by default; enable it with [prompt.interactive] toggle_enabled = true. It is bound after the vi keymap is set up, in viins + vicmd with vi_mode = true, else in emacs; it used to land in a keymap that bindkey -v then replaced, or steal emacs ^P.
    • Prompt code runs command git / awk / sed / …, so user aliases or functions with those names no longer change or break it.

    Generated init: one fast file (zsh/bash)#

    • core.<ext> is now the only generated file init.<ext> loads: what used to be lazy.<ext> ([tools] lazy loaders, tools.<ext>, extra.<ext>), login.<ext> (login-only tools, now inside if [[ -o login ]] / shopt -q login_shell) and helpers.<ext> (evalcache, zsh-defer) is inlined, and the startup PATH apply no longer reads path_sync.<ext> (the prompt hook still does). wayu deletes old lazy / login / helpers.<ext> files (and their .zwc) when it regenerates; anything that sourced them directly should source init.<ext> instead. Load order is unchanged.
    • zsh: compinit runs only in interactive shells (completion is a line-editor feature, and compinit was most of the cost of sourcing init in scripts and zsh -c); in other shells a no-op compdef is defined if none exists, so plugins calling it stay quiet. .zcompdump is also zcompiled (.zcompdump.zwc, in the background) — compinit loads it ~40% faster. The compiled file is installed only if the dump did not change while compiling, so a shell rebuilding the dump at the same time can't leave a stale .zwc that hides newly added completions.
    • zsh: the native prompt is set up in interactive shells only.
    • bash: the PATH apply no longer uses here-strings (a temp file each in bash 3.2) and compares in the C locale; the separate dedup pass is gone (the apply already leaves PATH without duplicates).
    • [tools] evalcache (zsh) finds the tool by walking $path instead of ${commands[...]}, which hashed every PATH directory (~2 ms).
    • Startup, 20 [paths] / 60 [aliases] / 20 [env] (tests/benchmark/startup.sh, macOS, hyperfine): zsh -f -c 'source init.zsh' 22.8 → 9.3 ms (empty zsh ~3.5 ms; turbo.zsh was 8.4 ms), interactive (zsh -fi, with compinit) 22.3 → 16.0 ms; bash 9.3 → ~5 ms (turbo.bash was 3.1 ms).
    • wayu build / build eval list core.<ext> and path_sync.<ext> only.

    wayu export#

    • turbo.<ext> now has exactly core.<ext>'s content — every feature ([tools] loaders, prompt, login tools, live PATH sync, completions with compinit) at the same speed — and wayu rewrites it whenever it regenerates core (any path/alias/const change, TUI edit, wayu build), so it no longer goes stale. Sourcing init.<ext> is equivalent; turbo stays for rc files that already use it. wayu export --turbo output text changed.
    • wayu export --eval expands [paths] values in the shell (like core): [paths] b = "$FZG/bin" with [env] FZG = "~/g" now works (it was dropped), an entry whose variable is unset is skipped, and entries are checked with [ -d ] when eval'd (not when wayu runs). Duplicates are dropped. The PATH part is now a short loop instead of one export PATH=.
    • wayu build no longer prints the turbo export report when turbo.<ext> exists (it is refreshed silently with core).

    fish (core.fish)#

    • [tools] now load in fish. evalcache entries run <tool> <args> | source, cached under ~/.cache/wayu/evalcache/fish__* (regenerated when the binary's path or mtime changes; needs fish 3.5+, older fish runs the tool uncached). Args are retargeted: a word zsh or bash becomes fish and --zsh / --bash becomes --fish, so args = "init zsh" runs <tool> init fish. eager, deferred (after plugins) and login_only (status is-login) work as in zsh/bash. A lazy entry needs a fish init_script (*.fish); nvm / conda recipes have no fish version and are skipped with a comment.
    • functions/*.fish load (they did only on the legacy path).
    • [paths] dirs move to the front of PATH in [paths] order, like fish_add_path -gpm: a dir already on PATH (e.g. /usr/local/bin) now gets wayu's priority instead of keeping its old place. Dirs wayu did not add are never removed.
    • Live PATH sync: wayu path add/rm and hand edits of [paths] reach open fish shells at the next prompt (a fish_prompt event handler re-reads the new path_sync.fish when the list changed), as in zsh/bash.
    • Re-sourcing init.fish no longer adds the completions dir to fish_complete_path again.
    • [aliases] are defined last (after plugins and tools), as in zsh/bash.
    • init.fish sources tools.fish before extra.fish (was the reverse). An untouched init.fish is updated automatically.

    zcompile#

    • A background compile interrupted by a signal removes its temp digest, and temp digests (<file>.<pid>.tmp.zwc) older than a minute are swept before compiling; the compile also runs in its own session, so closing the terminal no longer kills it halfway (stray core.zsh.<pid>.tmp.zwc files were left in the data dir).
    • Generated zsh files are recompiled in the background after every change (wayu path/alias/const add, TUI, …), not only by wayu init / build, so the bytecode speedup no longer disappears after the first edit.
    • wayu_compile (now defined in core.zsh) uses the data dir the file was generated for, and compiles core, plugins and turbo.
    • wayu build profile works when the data dir path contains spaces.

    Colors#

    • Output is plain (no ANSI escape codes) when stdout is not a terminal: wayu path list | grep x, $(wayu ...), logs and CI get plain text. Set FORCE_COLOR=1 (or CLICOLOR_FORCE=1) to keep colors in a pipe. Errors/warnings on stderr are colored only when stderr is a terminal.
    • NO_COLOR=1 and --no-color now remove every escape code (tables, help, errors, doctor, backup list, …); some used to remain. They win over FORCE_COLOR.

    Errors and warnings#

    • ERROR: … and ⚠ … messages go to stderr (they were on stdout), so 2>/dev/null silences them and wayu … --json | jq never sees them.
    • A failed read of a file reports one error, not two (the extra ERROR: Could not read … line is gone).
    • Before wayu init, path list|get|rm|clean|dedup and path add of an existing directory exit 78 with the "not initialized" message, like alias/const (they exited 66 with "File not found").
    • wayu export help / export list work without a wayu config.

    --json#

    • alias list --json, const list --json and plugin list --json print an empty JSON list ({"aliases": []}, …) when there is nothing to list; they printed ℹ No … found.
    • plugin list --json escapes every string (a quote or backslash in a path broke the document).
    • path list --json --source external (and --full) include the external $PATH entries the table shows ("source": "external"); they were dropped.
    • search QUERY --json prints {"query": …, "results": [{"type", "name", "value", "match", "field", "score"}], "count": N}; it ignored --json.
    • --json on a command/action without JSON output (path add, const get, hooks, toml show, …) exits 64 and names the commands that support it; it used to be ignored. Supported: path|alias|const| backup|plugin list, search, doctor (and any help).

    Commands and actions#

    • Command names, action words, per-command flags and --json support come from one table (also used by completions and wayu help). An action word a command doesn't have exits 64 with that command's help: e.g. alias check (silently did nothing, exit 0), alias clean (exit 1), backup clean|add|get, path enable.
    • wayu help lists every command (it missed build and export) and a COMMAND FLAGS section; --json and --no-color are listed under FLAGS.
    • Completions offer each command's flags and --json where supported, and export check.

    Tables and pickers#

    • List tables written to a pipe or file (wayu path list | cat) are no longer fitted to 80 columns: values are printed whole. An exported COLUMNS still sets the width.
    • The interactive picker (TUI remove, completions) keeps every character of a paste or fast typing (only the first one was used), ignores unknown escape sequences instead of filtering on their bytes, and a lone Esc cancels like Ctrl+C. kill -INT / kill -QUIT restore the terminal.

    TUI terminal handling#

    • Keys: Esc followed by a key within 100ms is now Alt+key (what terminals send for Meta/Option chords) and does nothing; it used to be "Escape, then the key", so Alt+d in the filter cancelled it and opened a delete confirmation. A lone Esc therefore takes effect after 100ms (was 25ms), which also keeps arrow keys split by a slow ssh link from acting as Esc. ESCDELAY (milliseconds, as in ncurses) changes the window.
    • Paste: bracketed paste is enabled while the TUI runs. A paste goes into the focused text field (add form, filter) as text — newlines dropped, tabs as spaces — and is ignored anywhere else; pasted newlines and letters no longer submit forms or run actions. In terminals without bracketed paste, keys typed ahead of a delete confirmation or after a submitted form are discarded, so the rest of a pasted line can't answer the dialog.
    • Ctrl+Z suspends the TUI (and kill -TSTP restores the terminal before stopping); fg resumes and repaints. Ctrl+Z used to be ignored.
    • Colors: list text uses the terminal's default foreground instead of a fixed light gray. On a light background — WAYU_THEME=light, a light COLORFGBG, or the terminal's answer to an OSC 11 query at startup (WAYU_THEME=dark skips the query) — dividers, orange/amber, green and blue accents use darker variants. In 16-color terminals the accent is bright magenta (was red, like errors) and dividers gray (were black). The hidden cursor is parked on the selected row for screen readers.
    • Width: combining accents, emoji variation selectors (VS16) and ZWJ sequences take no column of their own, and text-style symbols such as ➜ ✔ ★ ❤ ⛰ count as one column (they counted two), using the same Unicode tables as terminals. Rows with such characters no longer shift or leave stray glyphs in the TUI, and CLI tables containing them line up differently. In the TUI a VS16 or ZWJ is dropped, so ❤️ is drawn as ❤ and a ZWJ family emoji as its separate emoji.
    • If the TUI dies (a crash or a fatal error in shared code), what it wrote to stderr — the runtime's bounds-check location, the error before the exit — is printed after the terminal is restored; it used to be wiped with the alternate screen. An unreadable wayu.toml while adding or removing an entry is reported in the TUI instead of exiting with the terminal left raw.

    Editor (function add/edit, config edit|extend, hooks edit)#

    • $EDITOR / $VISUAL may carry arguments (code --wait, subl -w): it runs as sh -c '$EDITOR "$1"'. It used to be looked up as one program name and silently fail.
    • An editor that can't start or exits non-zero makes wayu exit 1 with ERROR: Editor '…' exited with status N (it exited 0 and printed "Reload your shell…"); config edit then skips regenerating the init.
    • With neither variable set, every command opens vi (function and config used nvim).

    Templates#

    • template apply never overwrites what you have: a [paths] directory already listed, an alias or [env] name already in wayu.toml, or a constant already set in the environment wayu runs in is kept and shown as Keeping …. (It used to replace e.g. EDITOR = "nvim" with code --wait.) The summary reads "N added, M kept".
    • --dry-run template apply … prints Would add … / Keeping … and "Nothing was written"; it used to print "… template applied!".
    • The developer template no longer adds code = "code ." (it shadowed the code binary).
    • wayu init --template <name> (or --template=<name>) works: init, then apply the template. An unknown name exits 65 and a missing one 64, before anything is written; any other argument to init exits 64.

    config scan --fix#

    • Aborts (exit 74) when extra.<ext> exists but can't be backed up or read; it used to write anyway.
