    • Blocks already in extra.<ext> are not appended again, so re-running it no longer duplicates PATH prepends and evals; with nothing new it prints "All N blocks are already in …" and writes nothing.

    5.0.0#

    doctor#

    • doctor --json (and --json doctor) prints JSON; --json --fix exits 64.
    • doctor exits 78 when any check reports an error (also with --json).
    • doctor --fix requires --yes (exit 64 otherwise); --dry-run --fix previews. It no longer symlinks ./wayu into /usr/local/bin or generates turbo files, and never removes a [paths] entry that uses an unset variable.
    • doctor --optimize is removed (exit 64); use wayu build / wayu export.
    • Startup detection covers ~/.zshenv, $ZDOTDIR, .zprofile, .zlogin, .bash_profile, .bash_login, .profile, fish conf.d/ and eval "$(wayu build eval)". wayu init writes $ZDOTDIR/.zshrc when ZDOTDIR is set.

    migrate#

    • Legacy import parses shell quoting exactly (single/double quotes, $'..', escapes, export A=1 B=2, typeset -x, fish set -gx/alias). Lines it can't convert exactly (functions, conditionals, multi-line values, command substitution, …) are listed with file:line; then nothing is imported or archived and it exits 65. Files are archived only after a full import.
    • migrate --from X --to Y no longer translates generated files line by line: it requires wayu.toml (exit 78 otherwise), sets [shell] type and regenerates the target shell's files from wayu.toml.

    Prompt (zsh)#

    • The native wayu prompt is now opt-in. It is generated only when wayu.toml has enabled = true under [prompt]; without it wayu no longer sets PROMPT/RPROMPT, setopt promptsubst, the vi keymap (bindkey -v), KEYTIMEOUT=1, the zle-line-init/zle-keymap-select widgets or its git/async precmd hooks. To keep the previous prompt, add:

      [prompt]
enabled = true

    • [prompt] text (format, character symbols, [prompt.contexts] formats, rprompt_format) is literal: $(...), backticks, $VAR and quotes are printed as typed instead of being executed or breaking core.zsh. Prompt % escapes (%n, %~, …) and the module variables ($dir, $user, $branch, $version, {git_pending}, …) still work.

    • toggle_key and [settings] autosuggestions_accept_keys are emitted as single-quoted bindkey arguments; a key containing ' no longer breaks (or injects code into) the generated file.

    • The async right prompt keeps its data in a private mktemp -d directory (mode 0700, removed when the shell exits) instead of ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/.wayu_async_<pid>.

    Watcher#

    • wayu watch no longer grows in memory while idle, and removes its watcher.pid when stopped with Ctrl+C / SIGTERM / SIGHUP.

    Plugins#

    • plugin rm on a plugin dir that is a symlink removes only the link; the link target (e.g. your working copy) is never touched. A plugin dir that resolves outside plugins/ is not deleted (warning; the entry is still removed from plugins.json).
    • plugins.json is validated on load. Any command that reads it exits 78 naming the bad entry when a url is not https://, ssh://, git@host: or file://, starts with - or contains whitespace/control characters; when a name, git.branch/tag/commit/pinned_ref or installed_path starts with - (or has control characters); or when shell, template, source_type or git.ref_type holds an unknown value. Enum values are matched case-insensitively ("shell": "bash" used to load as zsh) and plugins.json now stores them as names ("shell": "ZSH") instead of numbers; old files still load and older wayu versions read the new ones.
    • Plaintext http:// and git:// plugin URLs are refused (plugin add exits 65). ssh:// and file:// URLs are now accepted by plugin add.
    • plugin add <name-or-url>@<commit> (7–40 hex digits) installs at that commit and pins it; pinned plugins are skipped by plugin update, and plugin check fails if the checkout has moved off the pinned commit.
    • plugin check exits 74 and prints "N plugin(s) could not be checked" instead of "All plugins are up to date!" when any remote could not be read. It compares against refs/heads/<branch> exactly, so branches like release/main or a tag named main no longer cause false "update available" reports.
    • plugin update fetches and fast-forwards; when upstream rewrote history (force-push) a clean checkout is reset to the remote branch. A checkout with local modifications, or a symlinked plugin dir, is never reset — the update fails with git's error message, which is now shown. Output shows the old → new commit for each plugin.
    • --dry-run plugin update prints "Would update …" and no longer claims plugins were updated.

    Generated shell code#

    • [aliases] are defined at the end of core.<ext>, after plugins, lazy tools, tools.<ext> and extra.<ext>. Functions in those files can no longer rely on wayu aliases being expanded inside their bodies; an alias named like a wrapper (npm, conda, a lazy hook command) no longer breaks the tool loaders.
    • zsh init works under NO_BARE_GLOB_QUAL, KSH_ARRAYS and NO_GLOB, and with aliases for ls/rm/node/… defined before wayu is sourced.
    • The user-function loop variable f is no longer left set in the shell.

    nvm ([tools] nvm = { kind = "nvm" })#

    • The default node is resolved like nvm does: aliases are followed (lts/iron, lts/*, v20.18.0 with a leading v), the highest matching install wins (20 → newest 20.x, not the lexicographically last), and a partial version matches whole components (20.1 → 20.1.x only). Defaults that previously put no node (or an older one) on PATH now pick a different version. .nvmrc / .node-version (zsh) use the same rules.

    Completions#

    • zsh: when ~/.config/wayu/completions changed after ~/.zcompdump was written (e.g. wayu completions add), the dump (and its .zwc) is deleted and rebuilt with compinit -u; otherwise compinit -C as before.
    • bash: completions/*.bash is sourced too, so wayu completions generate (which writes wayu.bash) enables wayu's own bash completion.
    • wayu's own zsh/bash/fish completions cover every command (doctor, template, hooks, reload, build, function, aliases like const, fn, watch) and are generated from one table.

    init.<ext>#

    • init.<ext> is only updated when it is an unmodified copy of a template an earlier wayu wrote; the old file is backed up first. A file you edited is left alone and wayu prints a warning on stderr (once per edit when stderr is a terminal). To adopt the new template, move it aside and run wayu init.

    Flags#

    • Unknown options are an error: wayu path add DIR --dryrun (typo) exits 64 and writes nothing instead of performing the add. Each command accepts the global flags plus its own (doctor --fix, plugin update --all, migrate --from/--to/--schema, export --eval/--turbo/--check, …). A value that starts with - goes after -- (wayu path rm -- -odd); the first value word of alias add / const add (const add OFFSET -5) and negative numbers (plugin priority foo -1) are still taken as values.
    • A global long flag at the very end of alias add / const add (--dry-run, --yes, --json, --no-color) is now a flag, not part of the value: wayu alias add x y --dry-run previews instead of storing y --dry-run. To keep it in the value, put -- before the value: wayu alias add hd -- helm install --dry-run. A trailing -n / -y still belongs to the value (grep -n) but prints a warning on stderr.

    Hooks#

    • A {path} / {name} / {value} placeholder inside single quotes in hooks.conf is no longer substituted by wayu: it becomes "$WAYU_HOOK_PATH" (etc.) for an inner shell to expand. This closes a command injection through sh -c '... {path}', ssh, eval. A plain echo 'Adding {path}' now logs the literal reference — use double quotes (echo "Adding {path}") for direct substitution. wayu hooks flags such placeholders.
    • pre_* hooks run only when the operation will really write: not for invalid names, missing entries on remove, or duplicate path adds.

    Backups#

    • Every write now keeps only the newest 5 backups per file (previously only path clean/dedup pruned, so the backup dir grew without bound).
    • A command takes at most one backup per file (the state before it ran): migrate, template apply, doctor --fix no longer leave one backup per entry. The TUI still backs up every change.
    • wayu backup restore <type> [N|file] --yes restores backup #N from wayu backup list (or that file). The snapshot taken before a restore is marked [pre-restore], and a restore without N skips those, so repeating it no longer flips between the last two states; undo a restore with wayu backup restore <type> 1 --yes. backup list --json entries gain index and pre_restore.

    export / build#

    • wayu export --eval, --check and --turbo now do what the help says (they all used to regenerate the turbo file and print decorated output, so eval "$(wayu export --eval)" broke the shell). --check exits 78 when the turbo file is missing or older than wayu.toml.
    • wayu export list shows the formats instead of writing the turbo file; an unknown export mode or build target exits 64.
    • wayu export refuses fish (exit 64): its output is sh syntax. wayu build no longer refreshes a turbo file for fish.
    • Turbo/eval output does not include [tools] lazy loaders, the prompt, login hooks or live PATH sync; the help now says so (it used to promise a drop-in faster replacement). wayu build help no longer claims SIMD/threaded/GPU optimisation.

    4.4.4#

    Lookups and output#

    • wayu const|alias|path get NAME matches the exact name only (case-sensitive). A miss prints nothing on stdout, lists up to 5 similar names (never values) on stderr and exits 65. The interactive fuzzy picker and the WAYU_FFF_AUTO_FALLBACK / WAYU_FFF_INTERACTIVE toggles are gone.
    • Secret-looking values (names with KEY, TOKEN, SECRET, PASS, API, AUTH, …, or token-shaped values) are shown as ******** in --dry-run, search, export --dry-run and migrate dry-runs. const get and const list still print real values.
    • --dry-run on alias/const/path changes shows only the keys that change (+ / ~ / -), not the whole wayu.toml.

    Files and permissions#

    • Backups and generated files (core, lazy, login, helpers) are 0600, the backup dir 0700; older backups are tightened on the next backup. A new wayu.toml is created 0600; an existing one keeps its mode.
    • All writes are atomic (temp file + rename) and serialized across processes by ~/.config/wayu/.wayu.lock; concurrent wayu commands queue instead of losing entries.
    • A wayu.toml table holding an unterminated multi-line value makes edits fail with exit 65 and writes nothing.

    PATH#

    • [paths] is never re-sorted: file order is PATH priority. path add appends (lowest wayu priority, still ahead of system dirs).
    • Entries containing : or a newline are rejected (exit 65); such hand-edited entries are skipped with a warning.
    • The wayu() shell function is gone. Open shells pick up PATH changes — including hand edits of [paths] — at their next prompt via a prompt hook.
    • [paths] values are expanded by the shell: $VAR / ${VAR} work, an unset variable drops that entry, missing directories are skipped. [env] is now emitted before PATH so $GOPATH/bin works.
    • Removing an entry never strips a directory the system PATH also provides.
    • The legacy path.<ext> is no longer sourced once [paths] exists.

    Generation#

    • Plain wayu build regenerates every initialized shell's files (it used to run the turbo export; use wayu build turbo for that). Mutations also regenerate every initialized shell, not only $SHELL's.
    • wayu config edit regenerates after the editor exits.
    • wayu build eval emits code for the shell that evaluates it (its parent process), not $SHELL; under an unknown shell it prints nothing; as root on a user-owned config (sudo zsh sourcing your .zshenv) it writes nothing.

    Distribution#

    • Release binaries: macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64 only. Homebrew refuses other architectures with an architecture error.

    4.4.3#

    • $(...) in [env] values is kept literal; it no longer executes at shell startup.
    • -f, -n, -y after an alias/constant value are kept as part of the value; use -- to end flags explicitly.
    • Hook placeholders are passed env-quoted.
    • --dry-run writes nothing anywhere (no regeneration, no hooks).
    • backup restore requires --yes.
    • Exit codes: data errors exit 65, I/O errors 74.
    • Ctrl+Z no longer suspends the TUI.
